The third experiment, using high substrate and low catalyst concentrations, was designed to maximize the concentration of the `catS` complex relative to free `cat`. This was intended to distinguish between deactivation mechanisms dependent on `catS` (M17, M18) versus those dependent on free `cat` (M11, M12).

The results show that this experiment was highly informative. M17 remains the leading candidate, and its lead over the others has increased. M12 is now the second-best, while M11 has dropped to fifth place. This strongly suggests that deactivation is not primarily dependent on free catalyst under these conditions, which supports my hypothesis. The NLL values have started to separate significantly, with a clear group of top contenders (M17, M12, M18, M14, M11) and another group that fits the data much more poorly (M7, M4, M1, etc.). The aim of the experiment was largely achieved, as it successfully pruned the set of plausible mechanisms.

<hypothesis>
The top two candidates are now M17 (`P+catS=>inactive`) and M12 (`P+cat=>inactive`). Both involve product-assisted deactivation. The key difference is whether the product interacts with the catalyst-substrate complex (`catS`) or the free catalyst (`cat`).

My previous experiment (high `[S]`, low `[cat]`) created a situation with high `[catS]` and low `[free cat]`, which favored M17. To further distinguish between M17 and M12, I need to design an experiment that creates the opposite condition: high `[free cat]` and low `[catS]`.

This can be achieved by using a low initial substrate concentration and a high initial catalyst concentration.
*   With low `[S]`, the equilibrium `S + cat <=> catS` will lie to the left, meaning a large fraction of the catalyst will remain as free `cat`.
*   This condition will amplify the deactivation pathway in M12 (`P+cat=>...`) because `[free cat]` is high.
*   Conversely, the deactivation pathway in M17 (`P+catS=>...`) will be suppressed because `[catS]` is low.

By also including a moderate amount of initial product, we ensure that the product-assisted deactivation pathway is active from the beginning of the reaction. This will maximize the difference in the predicted deactivation rates between M12 and M17. If M12 is correct, we should see very rapid deactivation. If M17 is correct, deactivation should be much slower under these conditions compared to previous experiments where `[catS]` was higher.

This experiment is designed to be a direct test of the two leading hypotheses by creating a kinetic environment that is maximally favorable to one (M12) and unfavorable to the other (M17).
</hypothesis>
